name: Buffer preparation & hold suite
turndown: Set by vessel minimum working volume and impeller submergence; numeric ratio pending vendor minimum working volume (Q-049)
notes: Sized off diafiltration buffer demand. GAP pending diavolumes (Q-020).
sizing_corner: high diavolume count at low product titre - the buffer suite is driven by the DF demand, which is worst when UF concentrates least (Q-020, Q-017)

name: Ligation reactor
sizing_basis: Batch volume = product mass / reactor concentration (P-CONC-LIG)
turndown: Set by reactor minimum working volume and impeller submergence; the formula and a measured reference ratio now exist (see notes) but the vessel is not selected, so no numeric ratio is committed (Q-049)
notes: Jacketed, temperature-controlled mixing vessel. Sizing GAP pending P-CONC-LIG, which is an upper bound on titre rather than a titre, so the volume it implies is a floor (Q-016). TURNDOWN JUSTIFICATION CORRECTED 2026-09-25: this row said turndown was set by 'low-shear mixing at low fill'. That has the sign backwards and rests on evidence that does not exist. Specific power in a stirred vessel goes as impeller speed cubed times diameter to the fifth over volume, so at constant speed REDUCING the fill RAISES specific power - low fill is the HIGH-shear condition, not the low-shear one. And no published critical shear rate exists for a short duplex at all: what exists is long-chain, a critical shear rate for T4 DNA at 166 kbp, about four orders longer in contour than a 21-mer, while naked 21-nt siRNA retained more than 80 percent band intensity through sonication, vortexing and atomisation (SRC-NAKED-NA-2023). Shear lability is a long-chain phenomenon, so the turndown gap was parked behind a constraint that is both mis-signed and unevidenced. A CAVEAT THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THAT ROBUSTNESS EVIDENCE: it was measured at 0.02 g/L, about three orders BELOW P-CONC-LIG, so it establishes that the molecule is robust and not that a concentrated polyanion solution is. What actually sets the ratio is geometry, and the formula is now in hand: minimum mixing volume equals width times length times the height to the edge of the impeller, so for straight sides the cross-section cancels and the ratio is simply fill height over impeller height (SRC-PALL-US9248420, verbatim formula; its own worked example gives 13 for a conventional bottom-mounted impeller and 25-36 for a high-turndown one). That reference is carried for the FORMULA and as an order of magnitude only, for three reasons stated rather than hidden: it is a single-use mixing bag and not a jacketed reactor, both of its ratios come from the same example in the same document, and the document is internally inconsistent about its own scale - the example says a 50 mL bag and 50 mL of water while its arithmetic uses 50 L. Its own MEASURED unagitated volume of about 4 L gives 12.5, not the 13 its calculation reports. No ratio is committed here until a vessel is selected (Q-049).
sizing_corner: TWO corners, and they are not the same one. (1) The LOW end of the ligation concentration envelope: batch volume is product mass over concentration, so the largest vessel corresponds to the lowest titre - and P-CONC-LIG is an upper BOUND, so the registered value is the optimistic corner and the vessel it implies is a floor with no upper bound registered at all (Q-016, Q-064). (2) The LARGE-BATCH end against the anneal ramp: specific jacket area falls as the cube root of volume, so the corner 'short anneal AND large batch' is unreachable in a jacketed vessel (CPL-006), and the two corners COMPOUND - a lower titre demands a larger vessel, which is exactly where the ramp fails (Q-065).

name: Clarification / enzyme-separation filter
sizing_basis: Throughput L/m2 for depth + clarifying filtration. The two branches of Q-050 load this item differently - an immobilised ligase is separated here, a soluble one arrives already denatured - and NEITHER branch puts the denature hold itself in this item (R-021)
turndown: Single-use elements sized per batch (swapped by size, not turned down); throughput pending flux data (Q-036)
notes: BRANCH-AWARE since 2026-09-21; it previously presumed an immobilised enzyme, which presupposed the answer to Q-050. IMMOBILISED branch: the ligase stays on its carrier and is removed here by filtration or centrifugation (see the filtration finding, R-002). SOLUBLE branch: the ligase must be denatured by an 85 C hold FIRST, and that unit DOES NOT EXIST in this register - this item is single-use depth media and cannot denature anything. Its absence is registered against Q-050 rather than invented, and the product-integrity risk it would create is R-021. Either branch: cell-free-extract routes raise the protein and endotoxin load arriving here (R-017), and the residual-protein figure that would qualify either one is blank (P-ENZ-CLEARANCE-LRV, Q-032).
sizing_corner: HIGH protein and endotoxin load at HIGH throughput - the cell-free-extract branch of Q-050 puts a whole proteome through this item rather than one enzyme (R-017), and the immobilised branch may be the wrong unit class entirely, since 40-90 um beads are a screen duty rather than a depth-media one (Q-036, Q-050)

name: UF/DF skid (TFF)
sizing_basis: Membrane area from flux (LMH) and batch volume
moc_candidate: PES/regenerated cellulose membrane; SS or single-use flow path
turndown: Set by minimum channel crossflow velocity and system hold-up volume; ratio pending membrane area (Q-036)
notes: MWCO well BELOW the product mass, not above it: an oligonucleotide should be at least twice the MWCO for robust retention (SRC-GRONKE-2023) and the vendor rule is a MWCO 3-6x lower than the molecule (SRC-SCHWARTZ-BPI-2003, SRC-PALL-TFF); the only siRNA optimisation study ran at 10 kDa (SRC-ZYDNEY-2025). The previously asserted '30 kDa upper limit' is struck (Q-035). Area GAP pending flux (Q-036).
sizing_corner: LOW flux at HIGH diavolume count - area scales with both and neither is measured for an oligonucleotide (Q-036, Q-020)

name: Evaporator
sizing_basis: Heat duty Q=U*A*dTlm; area from duty and U; plus a minimum-wetting-rate floor on feed per unit tube perimeter (turndown limit, R-013)
turndown: Set by the minimum wetting rate (P-EVAP-MIN-WETRATE): below it the film breaks into rivulets, so a small batch must recirculate rather than run single-pass (R-013, R-004)
notes: Short-residence type (falling/wiped/thin film) favoured to protect the duplex. Turndown is set by the minimum wetting rate (~0.10-0.22 kg/m/s for water; SRC-HUGHES-2024): a small batch cannot run single-pass and must recirculate (R-013, R-004). Type selection and U pending Q-018.
sizing_corner: LOW feed rate: the binding corner is the minimum wetting rate, not the maximum duty, because below it the film breaks into rivulets and the unit must recirculate (P-EVAP-MIN-WETRATE, R-013)
